title: Implement subnet health prober and conditional control-plane endpoint recreate
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: On private control plane installs we've observed rare but impactful failures during control-plane subnet replacements and endpoint re-creation. This PR adds a lightweight subnet health prober, a staged endpoint recreate policy with conditional checks, and test hooks to validate safe teardown/recreate sequences. The goal is to avoid noisy peering flap and stuck DNS records during upgrades and to provide operators a deterministic simulator to validate rolling control-plane network changes. Changes include Terraform module updates, Helm chart values to enable the prober, new reconciliation logic in the installer controller, and an upgrade/rollback helper script. Checklist: - [x] Add subnet-health-prober controller and Helm chart plugin - [x] Extend aws_vpc module with optional "safe_recreate" lifecycle and pre-flight checks - [x] Implement conditional endpoint recreate policy (only when prober OK OR operator override) - [x] Add a test simulator (integration harness) to exercise drain+recreate flows - [x] Update docs and release notes - [x] Add e2e scenarios to perf-canary and eval-harness Notes and scope: This is focused on control-plane endpoints (PrivateLink/ENI-style) and subnet lifecycle for multi-AZ private deployments. It does not change data-plane routing or tenant workloads. See Linear ENG-32456 for acceptance criteria and SUP-8721 for linked customer incident. Related PRs: reference terraform module bump in redwood-terraform and a follow-up chart values cleanup in pr-xx on redwood-helm-charts.

diff_summary: terraform/modules/aws_vpc/main.tf: add optional variable safe_recreate (bool) and new data source aws_subnet_health_check
installer/controllers/subnet_health_prober.go: new file, implements periodic probe (icmp/tcp health checks) and publishes metrics to prometheus, exposes API for preflight checks

installer/controllers/endpoint_recreate_policy.go: integrates prober result, implements staged recreate: (1) mark endpoint pending, (2) validate peering hooks, (3) drain egress ENIs, (4) recreate endpoint, (5) validate DNS propagation
charts/private-installer/values.yaml: prober.enabled = false by default, rollout.proberProbeInterval configurable
charts/private-installer/templates/prober-deployment.yaml: new Deployment + ServiceAccount + RBAC for probing targets
scripts/upgrade_rollback_helper.sh: added --dry-run and --simulate flags to run simulator before applying terraform
test/integration/drain_recreate_simulator.go: simulates AZ outage and verifies controller follows safe recreate path
review_comments: Marcus Nguyen: Nice separation of concerns. A couple of nit comments on logging verbosity in the prober and a question about the default timeout for tcp probes (should it be aligned with AWS ENI detach timeout?).
Aisha Patel: Responded - bumped probe timeout to 20s and added a prober.timeout value to Helm values for configurability.
Lena Ortiz: Can we make the prober permissions scoped to control-plane subnet tags instead of cluster-wide? Security review requested this change.
Aisha Patel: Updated RBAC to restrict target namespace and added annotation/tag filter logic to the prober. Also documented the permissions matrix in docs/private-deployments/subnet-recreate.md.
Ravi Shah: Found a race in endpoint_recreate_policy when simultaneous AZ replacements occur. Suggest serialize per-vpc lock or use leader-election per-vpc.
Aisha Patel: Implemented per-VPC reconciliation mutex and added tests to the simulator to validate simultaneous operations are serialized.
qa_notes: Manual QA: ran upgrade_rollback_helper.sh --simulate on a 3-AZ staging VPC; verified endpoint recreate only proceeded when prober reported healthy or operator override used. Observed Prometheus metrics: prober_probe_success_count and endpoint_recreate_attempts. Added a follow-up ticket to add Grafana dashboard (ENG-32512).
release_notes: Added a subnet health prober and a safe, conditional endpoint recreate workflow for private control-plane installs. Operators can enable the prober via Helm values and perform dry-run simulations with the upgrade helper script. This reduces risk during AZ subnet replacements and avoids transient DNS/peering flaps.
